title: Bank Earnings Just Gave the Market a Much Needed Confidence Boost | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman interprets strong bank earnings and benign credit quality as evidence against an imminent bank-led recession, while shifting his macro attention toward AI and private credit. He sees AI infrastructure spending crowding out software budgets, payment incumbents challenging Circle, and investment banking benefiting from AI financing. He distinguishes earnings beats from the guidance expectations that move shares.
assessment: The inspected IBM and JPMorgan disclosures support important operating observations, with qualifications about causality and adjusted results. The absolute claim that short Treasury values do not fluctuate is contradicted by the reserve-fund risk disclosure. Many other quarter-specific and causal claims remain unverified rather than being awarded accuracy credit. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
framework_points: Use nonaccrual trends at diversified banks as a concurrent credit indicator, while acknowledging that private credit and AI may lead the next downturn.
Compare returns on tangible common equity with price to tangible book.
Distinguish reported operating results from market expectations and forward guidance.
tools_and_charts: JPMorgan, Citi, Wells Fargo and Bank of America consumer/commercial nonaccruals for 2Q25, 1Q26 and 2Q26
Company quarterly EPS, revenue, guidance and share reactions
transcript_cautions: The brief biotech guest clip is a promotion, not a full attributable analysis.
Caption numerals around Goldman ROTCE and bank EPS are malformed; exact numbers require source audio or filings.
Eisman presents adjusted JPMorgan EPS and ROTCE without consistently naming the adjustment.
